newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: U.N. urges Colombia to outlaw self-defense groups.
newsitem.headline: U.N. urges Colombia to outlaw self-defense groups.

text.p: The United Nations has urged Colombia to outlaw peasant self-defence groups operating across Colombia, citing "alarming reports" about their role in its endemic political bloodshed.

Attorney General Jaime Bernal Cuellar said earlier this week that a decree issued in 1994, permitting the formation of peasant defence groups or rural militias, was constitutionally sound and that there was no legal reason to ban them.
But Almudena Mazarrasa, director of the U.N. human rights office that opened in Colombia in April, said in a statement late Friday that the decree should be revoked.

Senior military officials have staunchly defended the self-defence groups, known collectively as Convivir. But Mazarrasa alluded to frequent charges that they are allied to right-wing paramilitary groups and fighting a dirty war against leftist rebels and suspected rebel sympathisers.
In the interest of protecting "the civilian population within the context of Colombia's internal armed conflict" they should be banned, she said.

"The office (of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights) has expressed its concern to the Colombian authorities and it continues in its efforts to obtain official information clarifying alarming reports about the activities and probable violations of human rights and international humanitarian law stemming from the existence of the Convivir," Mazarrasa said.
Colombia's Constitutional Court is to rule next month on whether the decree legalising the formation of private armed groups should be revoked.
